ai.title: Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers
ai.brief: Backblaze tells Ars it won’t share users’ backup, storage files with advertisers. ” It also makes no mention of advertisers. ” They added: Notably, no “sensitive personal information,” such as social security numbers, credit card numbers, or “precise geolocation,” is shared with advertisers, the policy states. However, identifiers, commercial information, “Internet or Other Similar Network Activity,” and “geolocation data” may be “sold or shared for targeted Advertising” Customers can use this link to opt out of the selling or sharing of their personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising.

sec.title: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
sec.brief: In this article ARTEX: Publicly available AI-powered offensive security framework AI agent architecture Capabilities Identifying ARTEX network activity Identifying ARTEX system activity Mitigation and protection guidance Microsoft Defender detections Hunting MITRE ATT&CK techniques Since its release in July 2026, the AI-powered penetration testing framework ARTEX has been abused by many threat actors to accelerate their existing workflows related to network reconnaissance, credential attacks, and web application exploitation. As of November 2026, Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed both state-sponsored and financially motivated threat actors such as Storm-0940 , Storm-3358 , Onyx Sleet , Pearl Sleet , Crystal Typhoon, and Salt Typhoon integrating ARTEX into their tooling. In the past few weeks, we’ve reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation.
